syllabusTopics: Introduction and characteristics of aromatic compounds
Preparation of benzene from decarboxylation of sodium benzoate, phenol, and ethyne only

Chemical properties of benzene: addition reactions (hydrogen, halogen); electrophilic substitution reactions: orientation of benzene derivatives (o, m and p), nitration, sulphonation, halogenation, Friedel-Crafts reaction (alkylation and acylation)
Combustion of benzene (free combustion only) and uses

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Resonance replaces Kekulé's alternation with a single stabilised hybrid: two equal Kekulé contributors, bond order 1.5 everywhere, and 152 kJ/mol of measured resonance energy — the stabilisation that redirects benzene's chemistry from addition to substitution. Contributors differ only in electron placement; the hybrid never oscillates.…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Resonance: The Real Structure of Benzene Resonance is the theory that replaced Kekulé's alternating bonds: **benzene is a single hybrid structure — a superposition of several contributing forms — that is lower in energy than any one of them.** The resonance energy (≈ 150 kJ/mol) is the hybrid's stabilisation over its best contributor, and the o/m/p isomerism of disubstituted benzenes is…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Resonance defined:** when a single Lewis structure cannot represent a molecule, the real structure is a hybrid of several valid contributing structures; the hybrid is *one* compound, not an oscillation. - **Benzene's contributors:** the two equal Kekulé forms (major), plus charge-separated forms (minor); all C–C bonds bond order ≈ 1.5.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Equal-energy contributors maximise stabilisation - benzene's two identical Kekule forms are why its resonance energy is so large.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Resonance: one real hybrid superposed from valid contributing structures - not oscillation. Benzene: two equal Kekule forms (major) + charge-separated minor forms; all C-C bonds bond order ~1.5. Resonance energy ~150 kJ/mol = hydrogenation deficit 360 - 208.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Resonance always stabilises: the hybrid's energy is below that of every contributing structure.

rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Resonance Is Bookkeeping, Not Flickering - The molecule does not jump between Kekulé forms; it *is* the hybrid, all the time. Contributing structures are human bookkeeping — ways of placing electron pairs on a page — and the real structure is their weighted superposition.…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Isomerism as the Hybrid's Geometric Shadow - The delocalised ring has no fixed double bonds, but it *does* have fixed positions: 1 through 6 around a hexagon. Worked Example Types - **Type A — define and illustrate:** resonance with benzene's contributing structures and the hybrid icon. - **Type B — resonance energy calculation:** from hydrogenation heats, the 360 − 208 arithmetic. - **Type C — isomer counting:** enumerate o/m/p products for a given disubstitution.…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Benzene is sometimes one Kekulé form and sometimes the other":** it is always the hybrid — the forms are descriptions, not states. **"Resonance means the molecule is unstable":** the opposite — resonance *stabilises*; the energy of the hybrid is below every contributor.
